title: The earliest photo of a person probably shows a man getting a shoeshine
body: Louis Daguerre took View of the Boulevard du Temple from a window beside his Diorama in Paris at about 8 in the morning, between 24 April and 4 May 1838 (or possibly 1837). The street would have been busy with carriages and pedestrians, but the exposure took **four to five minutes**, so everything that moved left no trace. Two figures stayed still enough to register: a bootblack and his customer at the corner, though some have suggested the ‘bootblack’ is really a water pump. The plate is widely considered the earliest surviving photograph to include a human being.

slides.prompt: Paris at eight in the morning, yet the boulevard looks deserted. Why?
slides.answer: Anything moving during the 4–5 minute exposure vanished
slides.detail: Only two figures held still long enough to register: a bootblack and his customer, by most readings of the plate.

slides.heading: What was there, what was recorded

left.label: The street
left.text: A busy boulevard of carriages, carts and walkers at eight in the morning.

right.text: Empty pavements: anything that moved during a four-to-five-minute exposure vanished.

events.text: The plate is exposed at 8 am (possibly in 1837)
Presented to King Ludwig I of Bavaria as part of a triptych
Loaned to the Munich City Museum; a restoration attempt ruins it

slides.heading: A mirror world
slides.text: As with all Daguerre’s plates, the picture is a mirror image. There may also be faint traces of other people, a child at a window and a horse, but only the two figures at the corner are clear.
